title: From pacifist to talks of going nuclear: China shaken as Japan breaks 80-yr-old shackles
content: Japan is shifting away from its long-standing pacifist security doctrine, with increasing defense budgets and a major enhancement of military skills. The nation has restarted arms exports and is forming a dedicated intelligence agency. China perceives these changes as a profound provocation and an emerging strategy, sparked by modern threats and regional shifts in the geopolitical landscape.

title: Unhappy with $7bn collateral data centre bill in ‘America's Dairyland’, Oracle goes to court
content: Oracle challenges Wisconsin regulators over a massive collateral requirement for its new AI data center. The company faces significant annual costs due to strict credit rules for utility We Energies. Regulators aim to prevent local customers from subsidizing large tech infrastructure projects. This dispute highlights growing concerns over tech companies' financial commitments and infrastructure costs. Many states are now implementing similar regulations for major technology firms.

title: Jeff Bezos ex-wife MacKenzie Scott helped write a 'donation playbook' for Snap founder
content: Snap co-founder Evan Spiegel and Miranda Kerr have donated $550 million to erase medical debt. This significant contribution will benefit over 261,000 Californians facing financial hardship.  The donation follows a model pioneered by MacKenzie Scott, who has given billions to nonprofits.  The funds will be channeled through Undue Medical Debt, a prominent organization.  This initiative targets vulnerable residents, alleviating burdens of unpayable medical bills.

title: Who is Eric Bieniemy's wife? Mia Bieniemy shot at Virginia home

The Chiefs confirmed they are aware of the incident, while police continue investigating. Bieniemy’s immediate focus is supporting his family during this difficult time.

title: Inner Mongolia grassland finds unlikely shield in plant-eating insects
content: Research conducted over several years in Inner Mongolia has identified herbivorous insects as vital players in ecosystem stability. These plant-eaters manage the food web by producing varied population levels, which mitigate the risk of sudden food shortages for predators and safeguard plant diversity. This study challenges prior assumptions, underscoring the crucial function of herbivores in maintaining ecological balance and biodiversity.

title: California ocean is 4°C hotter as whales vanish and pelicans starve
content: The rising ocean temperatures off California's coast are creating serious repercussions for marine life. Whales are being pushed away from their traditional feeding zones, while seabird populations face starvation. Additionally, great white sharks are venturing closer to shore, posing risks to beachgoers. The rise in toxic algae blooms is further contaminating the ecosystem and impacting local fisheries, with these shifts connected to climate change and El Niño phenomena.

title: Latest Baker Mayfield report reveals Buccaneers' confidence in $47M QB

title: Puducherry offers up to Rs 40,000 to repair thatched homes of ex-servicemen: Who can apply?

Applications are processed offline through the Rajya Sainik Board.

title: Pickaxe Mountain revives the Kahuta question: Could India have hit Pakistan’s nuclear leap?
content: The West Asia conflict highlights Iran’s nuclear ambitions and US-Israeli efforts to block them. Pickaxe Mountain, housing hidden nuclear facilities, has become a focal point. Strikes on Natanz in 2025 echoed earlier pre-emptive attacks on nuclear programmes worldwide, from Allied raids on Germany’s heavy-water plant in WWII to Israel’s operations against Iraq’s Osiraq reactor (1981) and Syria’s al-Kibar site (2007). India, however, refrained from striking Pakistan’s Kahuta facility in the 1980s, a decision that enabled Pakistan’s nuclearisation. To avoid escalation, India and Pakistan signed a 1988 accord prohibiting attacks on nuclear sites. India now prioritises survivability through layered missile defence projects.

title: Missiles from cargo planes: The new strike idea that could interest India
content: Modern warfare increasingly relies on smart, autonomous weapons designed to disable an adversary’s ability to retaliate. India’s Operation Sindoor in May 2025 reflected this logic, beginning with strikes on terror infrastructure and expanding to Pakistani military assets such as radar sites, airbases and command centres. Even temporary damage to runways or radars can create operational gaps, enabling follow-on strikes. Launch platforms are critical: India fields BrahMos missiles from land, sea and modified Su-30MKIs, while Rafales carry SCALP missiles. To expand salvo capacity, the US developed Rapid Dragon, a palletised missile system for cargo aircraft, now evolving into Dragon Cart. Brazil’s C-390 project with Anduril explores similar concepts. Such systems could complement fighters by turning transports into “missile trucks,” boosting strike volume.
